{"type":"text","text":"# Work unit U-0002

Rules: convert_raw_pointers_to_smart_pointers

## Files in the unit

### include/inventory/cache.h

```cpp
#

edits.replace: std::map<std::string, std::unique_ptr<Node>> index_;  // owns the nodes

std::string evicted = victim->key;
        index_.erase(evicted);  // destroys the node

std::unique_ptr<Node> owned = std::make_unique<Node>();
    Node* node = owned.get();

arguments.summary: PriceCache's index_ owns its nodes through std::unique_ptr; the manual deletes are gone. The list links (prev, next, head_, tail_) stay raw, non-owning pointers.
review_notes: An evicted node is destroyed by index_.erase; its key is copied first, because erase(victim->key) would read the key of the node it destroys.
std::make_unique<Node>() value-initializes the node where new Node default-initialized it; every field is assigned right after, so behavior is the same.

{"type":"text","text":"# Work unit U-0003

Rules: convert_raw_pointers_to_smart_pointers

## Files in the unit

### include/inventory/item.h

```cpp
#i

edits.search: Item* Item::clone() const { return new Item(*this); }
Item* Perishable::clone() const { return new Perishable(*this); }

Item* original = new Perishable("cheese", 4.0, 2, 1);
    Item* copy = original->clone();
edits.replace:
std::unique_ptr<Item> original = std::make_unique<Perishable>("cheese", 4.0, 2, 1);
    std::unique_ptr<Item> copy = original->clone();

arguments.summary: Warehouse owns its items through std::unique_ptr and Item::clone() returns std::unique_ptr<Item>; the manual deletes are gone. Warehouse::add(Item*) and release() keep their raw-pointer signatures, because tests outside this unit call them.
review_notes: Public API: Item::clone() and Perishable::clone() now return std::unique_ptr<Item>; every caller (warehouse.cpp, item_test.cpp) is in this unit.
Warehouse::add(Item*) still takes ownership of a raw pointer and release() still returns one: order_test.cpp and warehouse_test.cpp call them and belong to other units.
item_test.cpp's CloneKeepsTheDynamicType releases its items with reset() where it deleted them, so the live-count check after them is unchanged.

edits.replace:

                                   const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Item>>& items);

edits.search:

std::vector<Item*> items = inventory::createItems(specs);
    Report* report = inventory::makeReport("stock", items);
edits.replace:
std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Item>> items = inventory::createItems(specs);
    std::unique_ptr<Report> report = inventory::makeReport("stock", items);

arguments.summary: The factory returns owning smart pointers: createItem and makeReport return std::unique_ptr, createItems a vector of them, and destroyItems clears that vector; the manual new and delete are gone.
review_notes: Public API: createItem, createItems, destroyItems and makeReport take or return std::unique_ptr instead of raw owning pointers; every caller (factory.cpp, factory_test.cpp) is in this unit.
The tests release their objects with reset() where they deleted them, so each object still dies at the same point; their assertions are unchanged.

## Files in the unit

### include/inventory/order.h

```cpp
#

edits.search:
// An order with a growable array of lines (managed by hand) and a non-owning
// pointer to its customer.
edits.replace:
// An order with a growable array of lines (owned through std::unique_ptr) and a
// non-owning pointer to its customer.

arguments.summary: Order owns its growable array of lines through std::unique_ptr<OrderLine[]>; the manual new[] and delete[] are gone, and the copy operations still copy the lines.
review_notes: order_test.cpp still passes new Item(...) to Warehouse::add(Item*), which takes ownership of a raw pointer; changing add to take std::unique_ptr<Item> needs warehouse.h, warehouse_test.cpp and order_test.cpp together, so these two calls are left for that change.
std::make_unique<OrderLine[]>(n) value-initializes the array where new OrderLine[n] left the unused lines' numbers uninitialized; only the first count_ lines are ever read.
